Theorem
[Mean value property for harmonic functions on $\mathbb E^n$] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0384, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0385 1. ch26:26.35\group Mean Value Properties

If $\Delta u=0$ in $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^n$, then \[ u(O)=\frac1{\omega _nr^n}\int _{B(O,r)}u\, d\mu _E \] whenever $B(O,r)\subset \Omega $.
Proof

\sketch Differentiate the average in (r). Two integrations by parts using $\Delta |x|^2=2n$ show that its derivative vanishes; its limit at zero is (u(O)).

□
